analysis.investment_thesis: CapitalNumbers is a debt-free, founder-led IT services firm with strong ROE (20%) and ROCE (26.5%) trading at a modest 8.91x P/E. However, revenue growth has decelerated sharply (only 2% in FY25 vs 28% 5Y CAGR), and small-cap IT consulting lacks the durable moat I typically require.
key_strengths: Debt-free balance sheet: borrowings down from INR 6 Cr (2020) to zero (2025)
High-quality returns — ROE 20%, ROCE 26.5%, FCF positive all 5 years
Cheap optically at 8.91x P/E with strong 74.67% promoter alignment
key_risks: Growth stalling: revenue grew just 2% in FY25 (100 vs 98 Cr); EBITDA contracted from 35 to 32
No durable moat — commoditized IT services competing globally against larger players
Equity jumped 67→171 Cr in FY25 (IPO dilution); INR 77 Cr investing outflow yet to prove ROI
red_flags: Operating income fell from INR 34 Cr (2024) to INR 30 Cr (2025) — first contraction in 5 years
Other income of INR 6 Cr in FY25 inflating reported profits post-IPO cash raise
Tiny market cap (INR 203 Cr) with minimal institutional ownership (FII 0.73%, DII 4.60%) suggests low liquidity/scrutiny
analysis.detailed_analysis:
On the positive side, this is exactly the kind of clean small business I appreciate: zero debt, 5/5 years of positive operating cash flow, ROCE of 26.5%, and a founder holding nearly 75%. The 5-year revenue CAGR of 28% and net profit CAGR of 39% show a real business was built, and 8.91x P/E is not demanding. FCF of INR 18 Cr on a market cap of INR 203 Cr is an ~9% FCF yield — respectable.

However, the FY25 numbers are concerning: revenue growth collapsed to 2%, operating income declined, and the INR 26 Cr net profit is flattered by INR 6 Cr of other income on the post-IPO cash pile. IT consulting is a business I understand, but small Indian offshore shops have no switching costs, no brand premium, and compete against Infosys/TCS/Accenture downward and freelancers upward. Without a widening moat or reacceleration of growth, the cheap P/E is likely a value trap. I would watch from the sidelines until two more quarters confirm growth has resumed.
